title: I just wanted to blink an LED
description: What started as a simple Raspberry Pi experiment became a practical journey through Linux, networking, and Docker deployment for .NET containers. This article walks through seven real challenges uncovered when shipping from laptop to device without cloud abstractions.

title: Understanding Algorithmic Complexity - Part 2: From Theory to Practice
description: Part II turns complexity theory into hands-on practice with real C# refactoring scenarios, measurable performance differences, and runnable examples. It shows how to validate Big O assumptions in real code and make better design choices as data scales.

title: Understanding Algorithmic Complexity in Everyday C#
description: Performance issues often appear only when data and traffic grow. This article explains how algorithmic complexity shows up in everyday C# code, why clean-looking logic can degrade under load, and what to watch before simple operations become bottlenecks.

title: Part II - When Working Code Turns Against You
description: This follow-up explores bugs that hide behind apparent success: async flows that stall, tasks that ignore cancellation, duplicate queries, and serialization mismatches that surface only under real production conditions. These failures are dangerous because code can look correct while quietly bending system behavior.

title: Bugs We All Write (Part I): The Ones That Should Have Been Simple
description: Most costly bugs are not complex; they are small mistakes hidden in code that looked correct at first glance. This article explores why snippet-driven and AI-assisted coding can amplify these issues when we skip understanding the why behind the code.

title: The Hidden Cost of Convenience: Misusing Dependency Injection in C# Projects
description: Shortcuts like passing IServiceProvider through layers can speed up coding in the moment, but they hide dependencies and weaken architecture. This article explains why that convenience increases complexity over time and how to keep C# systems testable, maintainable, and easier to evolve.

title: From Smooth to Stuck: Diagnosing .NET Systems That Choke Under Load
description: Modern .NET systems often appear healthy — low CPU, stable memory — even as users experience slowdowns. The root cause? Thread starvation, async backlog, and invisible queuing due to IO pressure, memory retention, and overworked thread pools.

title: From Local Certainty to Distributed Chaos: Handling Consistency and Integrity in .NET Systems
description: In local systems, a transaction is enough to ensure consistency. In distributed systems, it isn't. This article walks through how to evolve from simple DbContext.SaveChangesAsync() logic into robust patterns like execution strategies, the Outbox pattern, and idempotent consumers. You'll learn how to preserve integrity across retries, external calls, and scale — without relying on distributed transactions. Real .NET code included.

title: From Vague Requests to Valuable Stories: A Scrum Master's Journey in Product Discovery
description: This post captures some of what I've been learning while working as a Scrum Master — a role that continues to offer insights I find valuable beyond delivery, especially when bridging product understanding with technical decision-making.

title: Designing with LLMs: Building a Prompt Pipeline Architecture
description: Over the past few months, we've seen a surge in applications that integrate Large Language Models (LLMs). While getting started with models like OpenAI's GPT or locally hosted options like Ollama is relatively easy, building real, scalable applications with LLMs requires more than sending a prompt and waiting for a response.

title: Manage Pull Requests
description: Pull requests is one important milestone when delivering software, especially if you are delivering software using CI/CD approach. It is a point in time where the team is able to share, learn, deliver and improve the product or the project they are delivering to the business.
